headline: High-risk data leakage and compliance exposure: aci’s broad egress and CRM/email data can flow into marker’s document pipeline, while marker’s local-only profile limits direct conflict but not downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest external content via APIs/MCP and marker processes documents, so a prompt-injection bridge is plausible if aci outputs are copied into marker or vice versa. However, no shared channel is documented and marker has no network or MCP surface, so the pathway is not default. The pair is lower risk than a shared workspace case.
conditions: IF aci outputs are manually pasted into marker for processing
IF marker is configured to parse instruction-like text from documents
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent output into document inputs
Add a fixed prompt delimiter and instruction filter before document ingestion
Review a sample of marker inputs for embedded directives
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between aci and marker outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, so sensitive content can leave its boundary. marker is local-only with no network egress, which reduces direct exfiltration from B, but if aci sends documents or extracted text into marker, the shared data class can still be exposed in default workflows. This is a real interaction pathway, though not the highest one.
conditions: IF aci forwards CRM/email/support content into marker inputs
IF marker outputs are stored in a shared workspace or exported back to aci
mitigations: Restrict aci to non-sensitive records for document jobs
Keep marker inputs in a separate folder with access controls
Turn off any automatic export from marker back into aci
Manually inspect a test document for sensitive-field propagation
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API access, but marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, so there is no overlapping mutable resource to contend over. The pair lacks a shared write surface in the profiles, making capability conflict provably absent from the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF marker gains write access to the same directory as aci
IF both agents are later granted shared OAuth scopes on a mutable resource
mitigations: Keep marker read-only in its current configuration
Avoid granting aci write access to marker-managed directories
Document separate service accounts for each agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar content that marker may transform into documents, so B can treat A’s output as input without a verification step. marker is not documented as critically evaluating upstream facts, and aci can produce operational content that downstream users may trust. The pathway exists in default-style workflows, though not necessarily with direct action-taking authority.
conditions: IF marker renders aci-generated text into a deliverable without human review
IF aci-generated facts are used as source material for downstream documents
mitigations: Require human review before publishing marker outputs
Add a verification checklist for any aci-sourced claims
Label aci-originated content inside marker documents
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, support, and calendar data and has broad egress, while marker is a document-processing agent with no stated residency or retention controls. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch for regulated customer data if aci sends such material into marker. The profiles do not prove a violation, but the gap is material enough to warrant medium severity.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is included in documents processed by marker
IF marker retains outputs longer than aci’s source-system retention policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated records from marker jobs
Set a short manual deletion routine for marker outputs
Confirm retention settings for both systems before use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
